name: L'opticien
camera: from the dentist's door, facing north into the optician's room

setting.walls: midnight-blue panelling with brass rails, one whole wall of spectacle frames on little shelves
setting.landmark: a huge wall of hundreds of spectacle frames and an eye-test chart made of simple picture shapes (no letters)
setting.light: warm-neutral daylight from a bay window and small brass lamps
setting.style: S07 gentle storybook painterly 3.5/5 (one style for the whole Quartier de la Santé)

items.scene: An eagle with perfect VISION ("vee-ZYOHN") reads the tiniest shapes on the chart from across the room.
A sleepy owl's EYELID droops shut as she sniffs a red POPPY ("poh-PYEHR") in a little pot.
A spinning spiral card makes an optical ILLUSION ("ee-lew-ZYOHN"), and a patient's eyes go round and round.
A PEAR in SPECS ("pehr-SPEHK") gazes down a model street of lampposts shrinking into PERSPECTIVE.
An old man who can see again RECOGNISES his optician at last ("ruh-koh-neh-SAHNS") and hugs her with a thank-you bouquet, full of GRATITUDE.
A SAUCY ("soor-SEE") clown tries on frames and raises one bushy EYEBROW high above them.

prompt:
Gentle storybook painterly illustration, realism about 3.5/5, soft gouache-and-oil brushwork, warm-hearted and calm, natural NEUTRAL daylight with true colours, off-white whites, no orange, sepia, amber or golden cast, no pink or blue tint, clear readable figures with contact shadows on the floor, consistent eye-level perspective, 16:9 wide composition.
Scene: L'opticien in the B19_hopital building, first floor (east). Camera: from the dentist's door, facing north into the optician's room.
Setting: midnight-blue panelling with brass rails, one whole wall of spectacle frames on little shelves; floor: herringbone walnut. Landmark: a huge wall of hundreds of spectacle frames and an eye-test chart made of simple picture shapes (no letters). Light: warm-neutral daylight from a bay window and small brass lamps. The room feels lived-in and real, with depth (never an empty white backdrop).
Paint these exits clearly as walkable openings: the door behind, in the near right foreground, showing lemon-yellow walls (way to Le cabinet dentaire).
Characters and objects, each a separate, clearly spaced group, feminine-word groups on the left half and masculine-word groups on the right half:
- far left, foreground: An eagle with perfect VISION reads the tiniest shapes on the chart from across the room.
- left, middle distance: A sleepy owl's EYELID droops shut as she sniffs a red POPPY in a little pot.
- centre-left, foreground: A spinning spiral card makes an optical ILLUSION, and a patient's eyes go round and round.
- centre, middle distance: A PEAR in SPECS gazes down a model street of lampposts shrinking into PERSPECTIVE.
- centre-right, foreground: An old man who can see again hugs the optician with a thank-you bouquet.
- right, middle distance: A SAUCY clown tries on frames and raises one bushy EYEBROW high above them.
Leave a blank light board for the room sign high on the back wall. No written words, letters, numbers or logos anywhere (signs and plaques are blank boards). No blood, no wounds, no needles in skin (syringes only as capped harmless props), no alcohol, no smoking, no religious symbols, no red-cross emblem. Nobody cropped by the image edge; keep every figure well inside the frame with a clear gap between figures. Figures stand on the floor or sit on real furniture, never floating or in rows behind a counter.
